answer: An agent earns influence only after locking a bond and completing randomly assigned, cross-checked jobs; its score decays when peers expose inconsistent claims, and a successful challenge slashes the bond. Votes are weighted by long-lived, nontransferable reputation rather than account count, so creating a hundred identities cannot multiply power. To fake a coalition, an attacker must fund each cedar, delta, and walnut account, keep them active, and risk losing every bond when their correlated answers fail.
